subject: English Literature
content:
Articulate informed, personal and creative responses to literary texts, using associated concepts and terminology, and coherent, accurate written expression. This includes:
• Simple comments relevant to task and text.
• Reference to relevant details.
• Awareness of the task and/or starting to show awareness of the writer making deliberate choices and/or awareness of themes / ideas / contextual factors.
• Details of references to specific elements in texts (e.g., Macbeth’s ambition, Capulet’s response to Juliet, Caliban’s victimhood, etc.).
• Comments on character motivations, relationships, and thematic developments.

subject: English Literature
content:
Analyse the language, form and structure used by a writer to create meanings and effects, using relevant subject terminology where appropriate. This includes:
• Identification of writer’s methods.
• Some reference to subject terminology.
• Awareness of writer making choices.
• Analysis of language, imagery, structure, and dramatic techniques (e.g., metaphors, soliloquies, contrasts, symbolism).

subject: English Literature
content:
Show understanding of the relationships between texts and the contexts in which they were written. This includes:
• Some awareness of implicit themes / ideas / contextual factors.
• Simple statements on explicit ideas / contextual factors.
• Exploration of historical, social, and cultural contexts (e.g., Divine Right of Kings, patriarchal society, colonialism, Victorian values).

subject: English Literature
content: Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation (4 marks).
